text:
sam: Hey @people-ops quick scenario: partner and I might travel to Spain after the baby is born. Thinking 8 weeks total, split as 4 weeks paid (US) then 4 weeks unpaid in Spain. Questions: 1) Will paid US leave still process if I'm physically in Spain? 2) Payroll/tax implications for the unpaid Spain segment? 3) Impact on mid-Dec performance review and equity vesting? 4) Can I keep laptop + hotspot there for the 8 weeks?

michelle (People Ops): Congrats! TL;DR: paid leave processes if you're still active and manager approves; cross-border stints need Payroll review; reviews still happen on schedule and vesting typically continues; equipment travel OK with IT ticket. We'll need you to submit the parental leave form and mark the international segment.

jules (Payroll): Hi Sam  short stays (<90 days) we usually keep US payroll/withholding but need proof of temporary travel and no local work. If you perform work or stay >90 days, local payroll registration may be required. Fill the International Payroll Intake so we can do a nexus check.

an a (Manager): Sam  I'll approve pending docs. For the review: lets schedule a 30-min calibration before Dec 10 if possible. Even if you're on leave we'll complete feedback on the normal cadence.

sam: What exact docs Payroll needs for the temporary-abroad case? Passport? Itinerary? Lease?

jules (Payroll): Passport copy + travel itinerary showing return date + a short signed declaration you're not working locally. If you plan to do any paid work, let us know now. I'll DM the checklist and intake link.

michelle (People Ops): Policy excerpt: "Paid parental leave is available to eligible US-based employees. International travel while on leave is permitted but must be disclosed. Cross-border work while on leave can create local payroll obligations." Benefits (health) typically continue but confirm premium payments while abroad.

sam: I won't be working during the unpaid Spain weeks but might glance at email. Is that considered working?

jules (Payroll): Occasional email checks are usually fine. Active contribution (deploys, support rotations) is considered work and could trigger local obligations. If you expect any such activity, mark it on the intake form.

it-bot: Reminder: open Equipment Travel ticket at https://redwood.internal/it/equipment-travel. Allow 10 business days for export/insurance paperwork.

sam: Filed parental leave form and attached passport + draft itinerary (ref: 7Y2X). Opened IT ticket IT-5621.

jules (Payroll): Received intake. We'll run a nexus check and post back by Nov 30. If local registration is needed we'll advise on withholding/gross-up options.

michelle (People Ops): Action items: Sam  finalize dates and keep docs updated; Jules  run payroll check; Ana  schedule review prep before Dec 10. We'll not pause review or vesting by default.

an a (Manager): I'll put Dec 6 at 10am for a 30-min prep; Sam let me know if that conflicts.

sam: Thanks everyone  appreciate the help. I'll update by Nov 10.

payroll-bot: Reminder: complete International Payroll Intake by Nov 12 to meet payroll timelines.
